rootCause.summary: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-coverage/cross-reference-audit.ts's auditOperativeStateForUnits located a unit's covering OperativeProvisionView via exactly two match paths: `p.currentSourceNodeId === nodeId` (an exact-occurrence match) or `(p.sectionRef && unit.anchors[0]?.sectionRef && p.sectionRef === unit.anchors[0].sectionRef)` (a bare sectionRef string match). Both are structurally NULL for every AMBIGUOUS DEFINITION-kind OperativeProvisionView: buildProvisionView's DEFINITION branch never populates sectionRef at all (only SECTION-kind provisions do), and an AMBIGUOUS resolution leaves currentSourceNodeId null by design (no single physical occurrence was chosen). The function never consulted candidateSourceNodeIds - the field that holds exactly the real set of ambiguous definition-node identities amendment/types.ts's own OperativeProvisionView already carries whenever targetResolutionStatus !== 'UNIQUE'. The result: a unit anchored to one of the real, independently-confirmed ambiguous definition occurrences was entirely invisible to this audit, and reconciliation.ts (acting alone, with no override) could reach FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED for it - the exact 'confident but wrong' state Architecture Invariant #13 forbids.
rootCause.asymmetryWithSectionKind: The SECTION-kind equivalent (Chain 4 in the certification, re-confirmed unchanged by this fix) never had this gap, because SECTION-kind provisions DO populate sectionRef even when AMBIGUOUS, so the pre-existing sectionRef fallback already caught it. DEFINITION-kind failed open; SECTION-kind failed closed. This fix makes both fail closed identically.

fix.description: Extended the coveringProvision lookup in auditOperativeStateForUnits to also match `p.candidateSourceNodeIds.includes(nodeId)`. Because amendment/types.ts's own documented contract guarantees candidateSourceNodeIds is populated ONLY when targetResolutionStatus is AMBIGUOUS (always empty for UNIQUE or NOT_FOUND), this added branch can only ever WIDEN matching for a provision that is already non-RESOLVED (AMBIGUOUS implies status is at best OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL, never OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED) - it cannot manufacture a false match against a genuinely resolved, current provision. Once matched, the existing `coveringProvision.status !== 'OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED'` check already correctly fires (PARTIAL != RESOLVED), producing the OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED_FOR_UNIT finding this module exists to produce - no other logic branch needed to change. The finding's own reasoning string was extended to name candidateSourceNodeIds explicitly when this new branch is what matched, for reviewer clarity.
fix.minimalityNote: This is precisely the smallestRemediationBoundary the certification itself named: 'Extend the coveringProvision lookup to also match against candidateSourceNodeIds for AMBIGUOUS provisions.' No change was needed to buildProvisionView, computeOperativeContractState, or applyOperativeStateFindingsToCoverage - the operative-state layer itself was already honest (confirmed by the certification's own Chain 2 evidence); only the ONE lookup that failed to consult evidence the layer below it already produced needed fixing.

unitTests.describeBlock: BLOCKER-6 fix: AMBIGUOUS DEFINITION-kind provisions are now matched via candidateSourceNodeIds
cases: flags OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED_FOR_UNIT for a unit anchored to one of an AMBIGUOUS DEFINITION-kind provision's real candidateSourceNodeIds, even though currentSourceNodeId and sectionRef are both null
the OTHER real ambiguous candidate node is flagged too - never only the first one checked

never widens matching for an already-RESOLVED provision - candidateSourceNodeIds is empty whenever targetResolutionStatus is UNIQUE, so this fix cannot manufacture a false match (a direct proof of the minimality claim above)

crossModuleChainReproduction.note: Chain 2 - the certification's own end-to-end reproduction - was extended in place per the task's own instruction (a test file, explicitly named as safe to build on). The chain was re-run through the REAL, now-fixed auditOperativeStateForUnits and rewritten to prove full composition: (1) the real ambiguity is now flagged (findings.length === 1, findingType OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED_FOR_UNIT, reasoning mentions candidateSourceNodeIds); (2) reconciliation.ts ALONE (a different module, correctly out of this blocker's scope) is confirmed to STILL independently reach FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED in isolation - proving the override below is doing real work, not vacuously passing; (3) applyOperativeStateFindingsToCoverage now correctly OVERRIDES that to OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED before it becomes the unit's final coverage state; (4) a real ClaimReviewItem is now persisted to Postgres for this exact claim (status OPEN_REVIEW, correct structuralNodeId) - where before this fix NO review item was ever created for it (a true silent-failure gap, not merely a triage-quality one). Chain 2's own verdict label in the test file was updated from BREAKS to COMPOSES; Chains 1, 3, and 4 were re-verified to still pass completely unmodified.
